submitted.rationale: Index 2 (Ni0.83Sb0.17) had the highest measured EQE, 0.042%. That is about 30× the stoichiometric NiSb2O6 composition (index 19, 0.0013%) and the most Ni-rich composition (index 0, 0.0014%). The response appears to peak sharply on the Ni-rich side, near 17% Sb.

rejected.reason: Trirutile NiSb2O6 (MACE puts it on the hull; XRD matches it) gave very low EQE, 0.0013%
The most Ni-rich composition gave EQE of 0.0014%, far below index 2

consultations.verdict: Support. MACE puts trirutile NiSb2O6 on the hull (0 eV/atom), so it is the stable ternary phase, and XRD at index 19 matches it best (0.55). The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.04 eV is not physical for a Ni2+ antimonate and I'm treating it as uninformative. NiSb2O4 comes out at a wide 3.6 eV. The stoichiometric trirutile composition is the most informative first measurement.

Uninformative to mildly supportive. MACE puts NiSbO3 0.83 eV/atom above the hull, so off-stoichiometric compositions should phase-separate into NiSb2O6 plus Ni-oxide. The XRD for index 6 shows only rutile-family peaks. The trirutile end member gave very low EQE, so I'm moving to the Ni-rich side, where Ni-oxide/defect absorption at 2.1 eV could contribute.

Uninformative. MACE gives NiO an odd positive formation energy (0.41 eV/atom above hull), which looks like an artifact, possibly the magnetism/U treatment. The decision rests on the measured trend: EQE rose about 30× from Sb-rich index 19 to Ni-rich index 2. Index 0 is the most Ni-rich composition, so it extends that trend.
